background: The [Parity RPC trait at 55c90d4](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L28-L70) exposes nine distinct methods. They did not arrive as one indivisible feature: [multi-call was added in 2017](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/f157461ee19740c8d013bb9885d3aa0aa5f91a8a) and [block replay in 2018](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/df5d27d5163e8d6f6d00f4f8996ce384fcf804cf). The [OpenEthereum trace guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module) also distinguishes ad hoc execution from indexed historical filtering, which requires tracing to have been enabled. This history supports specifying method contracts separately; it does not establish that every modern client must implement every method.

The [2026 standardization issue](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890) records that Erigon, Reth and Nethermind expose the nine-method namespace, while Besu lacks individual replay and Geth has a different debug tracing API. The [draft PR](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/895) leaves method scope and support policy for review. An unimplemented method must remain distinguishable from an implemented lookup that found no records; whether the profile is optional or split between execution and historical search is still a policy decision, not client agreement.

[Besu #6597](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/6597) requested `trace_replayTransaction` for Blockscout. A Besu contributor said the core team did not plan to implement it because it is outside the Ethereum specification and suggested `debug_traceTransaction`; another user noted that exposing the `DEBUG` namespace on a public endpoint was undesirable. The issue was closed due to age in March 2025, without an implementing PR. This records the team's stated scope at that time, not a current agreement on this profile.

[Besu #11357](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/11357), opened 2026-09-23, asks the team to reconsider individual replay using this project's cross-client H01 evidence, or to state that core support remains out of scope. [Besu #9699](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/issues/9699) separately tracks pre-execution state changes that transaction replay must account for. Neither issue changes the behavior observed in the pinned builds.
items.next_step: Agree the optional-method/conformance model with client teams; no assumption of adopted optional status or Geth support.
items.rationale: A caller should be able to distinguish an unsupported operation from a valid query with no trace.
items.recommendation: Specify each method independently; make the implemented subset discoverable or explicitly declared. An unsupported method should return -32601, never a fabricated empty result. Add individual replay to Besu when practical rather than removing it from the common API.
items.title: Method coverage

background: Parity modeled `trace_get` as a [single `Vec<Index>` path returning an optional object](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L84-L93). Its [trace database compares the full path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L267-L286), so an empty path identifies the root rather than a flat position. Parity [fixed `traceAddress` handling in 2016](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/948b614f4072d89678810c34b5ae23a1eb7bdf00). Its [Index deserializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/index.rs#L23-L64) accepted hex and decimal strings, but not JSON number tokens.

The pinned [Erigon lookup](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L134-L149) also compares the whole path; [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L220-L242) uses the first supplied index as a flat position; [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L402-L424) returns a collection. The path and singular-result proposal follows Parity, but changing either client needs compatibility review.

Parity's [localized-trace serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L501-L535) writes `traceAddress` from `Vec<usize>` as JSON integers. The draft retains that output representation and uses hex quantities for request indices. The conversion belongs at the caller boundary, not in trace responses. Requiring minimal hex input deliberately narrows Parity's acceptance of decimal strings; tree-path meaning does not depend on the two directions having identical wire types.

Reth has since converged upstream: [#27366](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27366) selects `trace_get` results by tree path, and main at [861a5616](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L220-L242) compares the full path, keeping flat-position lookup only as an internal helper. Released 2.6.0 still uses the flat selector.
items.next_step: Choose the tree-path contract and align Reth/Nethermind; the positive nested discriminator is now available.
items.rationale: The lookup argument should identify the same path that traceAddress describes, with a singular result matching the method name.
items.recommendation: Treat the argument as one traceAddress path: [] is root, ["0x0"] first child, ["0x6","0x0"] a nested child. Return one trace object or null for a missing transaction/path. Keep output traceAddress entries as JSON integers; callers convert them to minimal hex quantities for trace_get input. Integer request entries return -32602.
items.title: trace_get selector and return shape

background: Parity's [original matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L42-L111) treats each address list as alternatives, combines sender and recipient with `&&`, and builds the Cartesian product of address blooms for indexed search. An empty list matches all addresses. The [RPC filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L28-L68) had no `mode` field and rejected unknown fields. Thus intersection follows the Parity implementation, while explicit union is a later Erigon compatibility extension, not an original namespace option.

In [Erigon #2119](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/2119), banteg asked in June 2021 for an intersection option to narrow calls from a sender set to a recipient set. Erigon merged the [mode implementation in #3167](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3167) in January 2022, corrected the list-level boolean composition in [#3304](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3304), and [backported it to stable in #3305](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/3305). This is established client precedent for retaining an explicit mode.

[Alloy #4216](https://github.com/alloy-rs/alloy/pull/4216), merged on 2026-09-22, cites H03 and changes the default from union to intersection while retaining explicit union. Its tests cover OR within each list, AND between lists, empty lists, and both recognized modes. Reth uses [Alloy's matcher](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L354-L371), but the tested Reth builds and [main@47c2166bc4](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/47c2166bc48bba25b95787c1f0640ec42bb9dee0/Cargo.lock) (checked 2026-09-23) still lock Alloy 2.4.2, which predates the PR. Reth needs dependency uptake and a retest before its observed result changes.

The pinned draft accepts recognized modes. The mode cases were recaptured on 2026-09-23 against every tested build, including one-sided `union` queries. The Geth draft fork adopted recognized modes and nullable address lists at [40eecf3647](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/commit/40eecf3647f26546df9dbf72ce48f372df469ef2). Reth's null-list rejections are tracked under [H04](H04.md).

Nethermind master has no `mode` property at all ([TraceFilterForRpc.cs](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/ac02224f25fd4901116ebf2643d522ec4a0e60a1/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceFilterForRpc.cs#L10-L24)), and its matcher is intersection-only. That explains both observations: union behaves as intersection, and an unrecognized value is accepted because nothing reads it. The Nethermind change is therefore to add a validated field, not to reimplement matching.
items.next_step: Confirm the default and the two recognized modes with client teams. Retest Reth after it picks up Alloy #4216.
items.rationale: Adding a second filter should narrow a search. This matches `eth_getLogs`, where each topic position accepts a list of alternatives (OR) and all positions must match (AND); a null position is a wildcard, just as an omitted or empty address list is here. Explicit union is still useful when callers need one globally paginated result across both address sets.
items.recommendation: Use OR within each address list and AND between `fromAddress` and `toAddress` by default. An omitted, null, or empty side imposes no restriction. Accept optional `mode: "intersection"` (the default) and `mode: "union"` (match either populated side); reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.
items.title: Filter composition and mode

background: Parity's [RPC filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L28-L67) made both address arrays optional and converted an omitted or JSON-null field to an empty vector. Its [address matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L28-L63) explicitly treats that vector as matching all addresses; the bloom path gives it an unrestricted bloom rather than a zero-match search. This is an inherited API convention, not merely an intuition about empty filters.

The modern clients differ at both input decoding and matching. The pinned [Nethermind matcher](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TxTraceFilter.cs#L56) and [Erigon filter](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L311) must be read together with the linked empty/null cases: accepting a JSON field does not prove it is treated as unrestricted. H03 determines how nonempty sides compose; this decision only establishes when a side has no constraint.
items.next_step: Review the compatibility choice to accept null alongside omitted and empty lists; retain separate checks for special-action membership.
items.rationale: Programmatically adding an empty optional filter should not erase all results.
items.recommendation: Treat an omitted, null or empty address list as no restriction. A nonempty list restricts that side. Compare address bytes independently of hex letter case.
items.title: Empty address lists

background: Parity [added reward traces in 2017](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/06862c7dee400e3b9f37c6cfdae52c081ee9d7f1) for consensus payouts and then [made transaction IDs optional](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/1f3f91136ca9438336e5eb824ce31555ac116fae) because a reward is not a transaction. Its [serializer test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L814-L831) expects a `reward` action with null transaction localization. This explains why the trace model has non-transaction records at all.

[EIP-3675](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#block-and-ommer-rewards) removed the PoW block and ommer balance increases at the Merge while leaving transaction fees in place. [EIP-4895](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4895) later introduced withdrawals as block-level balance changes, but neither Parity's reward encoding nor that EIP defines a `trace_*` withdrawal action. The observed Besu and Nethermind zero-value reward placeholders therefore should not be treated as actual post-Merge rewards; whether to include withdrawals or other system changes needs an explicit separate trace contract.

Erigon already ships an opt-in representation ([PR #21592](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/21592), 2026-06-28). With the extra `traceConfig.includeWithdrawals` argument, `trace_block` appends `reward` records with `rewardType: "withdrawal"` and the value in wei ([trace_filtering.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L252-L256)), and `trace_replayBlockTransactions` appends an extra envelope without a transaction hash that carries the withdrawal stateDiff ([trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L1015-L1062)). It is off by default and absent from `trace_filter`. The extension lies outside the baseline: the draft’s `rewardType` enum is `block`/`uncle`, and a baseline replay array holds exactly one envelope per transaction.

No client emits records for EIP-4788, EIP-2935, EIP-7002 or EIP-7251 operations. Reth runs `apply_pre_execution_changes` untraced, Nethermind uses `NullTxTracer` for system calls, Erigon runs `InitializeBlockExecution` untraced and skips `txIndex == -1` in filters ([trace_filtering.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L746-L752)), and the Geth draft replays transactions only. The draft previously stated the exclusion only for withdrawals; stating it for system operations keeps anyone from later adding them as call frames with null localization, which would shift pagination.

Reward order is already uniform: the block reward first, then uncle rewards in ommer order, after the block’s transaction records. Parity appended rewards as a trailing pseudo-transaction ([db.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L189-L193)), Besu inserts the block reward at index 0 of its reward list ([RewardTraceGenerator.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/RewardTraceGenerator.java#L95-L102)), and Erigon, Reth and the Geth draft follow the same order. The PoW block-47 evidence agrees on all nine builds.

Genesis handling differs. Reth’s `trace_block` appends a reward whenever `calculate_base_block_reward` returns one, and that function has no genesis guard ([trace.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L307-L318)); on a PoW-genesis chain such as the `forks` fixture it reports a 5-ETH genesis reward that never happened, and `trace_filter` from block 0 includes it. Nethermind’s `trace_block(0)` fails because the genesis parent lookup fails ([TraceRpcModule.cs](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/ac02224f25fd4901116ebf2643d522ec4a0e60a1/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L367-L371)); this is still true on current master, and a fix is being prepared. Erigon, Besu and the Geth draft return `[]`. Erigon’s filter path has no block-0 guard for the reward branch, so an address-less filter from block 0 on a PoW genesis may still emit a genesis reward (medium confidence, source only). No captured case covers genesis yet.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation left the placement of rewards and the status of system operations to a later decision ("specify which protocol operations belong in this namespace") and said nothing about genesis. The revision fixes all three: rewards follow a block’s transaction records in ommer order, genesis has no records, and system operations and withdrawals are applied to state but never emitted. Reward ordering and the system-operation exclusion match every tested client, so they move no client. The genesis rule moves Reth (a fabricated genesis reward on PoW-genesis chains) and Nethermind (`trace_block(0)` fails). Erigon’s opt-in withdrawal records remain a non-baseline extension. See [filter-selection §4, §8 and §9](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md).
items.next_step: Add genesis fixtures (trace_block and replay of block 0, a filter starting at block 0) and a reward-crossing pagination probe on the PoW `forks` chain. Keep Erigon’s opt-in withdrawal records outside the baseline unless a separate withdrawal contract is agreed.
items.rationale: A reward trace should correspond to a real protocol operation, not a zero-value placeholder that changes pagination. A fixed position for rewards and an explicit list of operations that are never records keep pagination offsets and replay arrays identical across clients.
items.recommendation: Do not emit a synthetic PoW reward on a PoS block. Historical PoW rewards follow all transaction records of their block: the block reward, then uncle rewards in ommer order, each with null transaction localization. The genesis block has no transaction or reward records, so trace_block(0) and trace_replayBlockTransactions(0) return [] and filters over genesis contribute nothing. System operations (EIP-4788 and EIP-2935 pre-block calls, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 post-block calls) and withdrawals are applied to replay state in protocol order, but they are not trace records and belong to no transaction’s stateDiff; replay arrays hold exactly one envelope per transaction. Keep transaction tips in transaction accounting.
items.title: Post-merge reward records

background: Parity's [trace lookup methods](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L2052-L2110) returned `Option`: absent transaction, missing trace data and disabled tracing could all become JSON `null`; [mocked RPC tests](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/tests/mocked/traces.rs#L83-L166) confirm null for missing trace storage. By contrast, its [ad hoc call path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L108-L127) raises an explicit state-pruned error when required state is absent. Separating absence from unavailability improves on a real historical ambiguity.

[EIP-1474](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#error-codes) names `-32001` Resource not found and `-32002` Resource unavailable. [execution-apis #636](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/636), merged on 2025-10-14, defines `4444` (Pruned history unavailable) for several eth/debug methods, including `eth_getLogs`. Extending that code to trace methods and pruned execution state is the proposal here, not an already adopted trace policy. A requested range must not silently become a partial search at the retention boundary. [Reth #27367](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27367) and the linked pruning cases show why unavailable state must not serialize as an apparent empty result.

[EIP-4444's JSON-RPC discussion](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4444#json-rpc-changes) notes that pruned indexing may prevent distinguishing an unknown hash from an old one. When this prevents establishing absence, return unavailable history rather than claiming `null` proves the transaction never existed. An absent path in a successfully obtained tree still returns `null`. Harmonizing missing individual replay to `null` is also deliberate: Parity's replay path used a transaction-not-found error, unlike its indexed lookups.

Nethermind master at ac02224f broke out of the `trace_filter` block loop and returned the records gathered so far when a block or its parent lacked state (`TryResolveParentForTracing`, [TraceRpcModule.cs](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/ac02224f25fd4901116ebf2643d522ec4a0e60a1/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L299-L346)); genesis has no parent, so every range starting at block 0 returned `[]`. That is the silent narrowing this decision forbids. [Nethermind #13677](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/13677) (2a3b2531, merged 2026-09-24) rejects missing state or parent up front and skips genesis in `trace_filter`. The captured development build 641592d2 contains it and returns the records for ranges from genesis; release 2.0.0 · bec830cd predates it and returns `[]`.
Reth main (861a5616) returns null for a missing individual replay ([#27364](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27364)); released 2.6.0 still errors.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation also used -32001 for unknown range endpoints. [execution-apis #875](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/875) (0a4179bc, 2026-09-07) since requires `eth_getLogs` to return -32602 when a bound resolves beyond the head or the bounds are reversed, and forbids clamping ([filter.yaml](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/465d1b98d43e94ff3d57e904fd7d4bea7f6b804c/src/eth/filter.yaml#L153-L160)); Geth implements it as invalid-params errors ([eth/filters/api.go](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/eth/filters/api.go#L39-L42)). The trace draft already mirrors getLogs for filter composition and defaults, so it now follows this contract too. On `a/missing-block-filter` (toBlock 0xffff at head 0x30) the change flips Besu, whose `FilterParameter.validateBlockRange` is shared with eth_getLogs and already returns -32602 ([FilterParameter.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/parameters/FilterParameter.java#L193-L209)), from differing to agreeing, and flips Reth and the Geth draft, which return -32001, from agreeing to differing. Erigon (`[]`) and Nethermind (-32000) differ under either rule. Reth main still returns `HeaderNotFound` for such bounds ([trace.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L381-L388)). Single-block selectors keep -32001, matching the eth/debug getters. See [filter-selection §1, §3 and §10](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md).
items.next_step: Choose an unavailable-history error contract. Extend the retention fixture to Erigon, Nethermind and Besu; the current pruning result is Reth-only. Add an explicit reversed range (fromBlock 3, toBlock 2).
items.rationale: Not found, empty, unsupported and unavailable are different states that callers need to distinguish.
items.recommendation: Return null for a well-formed lookup of a transaction that is not in a canonical block, or of a missing trace path, consistently across these methods. Reserve [] for a successfully evaluated collection with no elements. Preserve -32601 for unsupported methods and use errors for unavailable/pruned state instead of pretending data is absent. An unknown single selected block (trace_block, trace_replayBlockTransactions, the trace_call/trace_callMany block) returns -32001 (Resource not found). trace_filter bounds follow eth_getLogs: if either bound resolves beyond the current head, or fromBlock resolves above toBlock, return -32602 (Invalid params); never clamp the range or return a partial result. earliest means the lowest available block; an explicit number below retained history returns 4444. If pruned indexing prevents establishing whether a hash is absent, return 4444 rather than a definitive not-found result.
items.title: Missing transactions and paths

background: [Parity issue #8725](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/issues/8725) reported that `trace_replayBlockTransactions` returned per-transaction state diffs without hashes, forcing callers to pair array positions with block transactions. [The 2018 fix](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/526c61e2c053f7ef98be93b118120ab585f4aaad) added a distinct `TraceResultsWithTransactionHash` type for block replay. The [Parity RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L59-L70) and [response structs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L671) retained a plain `TraceResults` for individual replay, whose request already supplies the hash.

The [OpenEthereum examples](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module) include `transactionHash` in block-replay items but omit it in individual replay, as does the pinned [Reth implementation](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs). Requiring it in both is an intentional additive contract improvement: each replay result remains identifiable when cached, forwarded or detached from the request. The benefit is consistent self-contained envelopes, not restoration of the original individual-replay shape. Clients and strict decoders need compatibility review.
items.next_step: Confirm the envelope schema and add one serialization test; treat missing support in Besu separately under H01.
items.rationale: A replay object should keep its identity when stored or moved out of its original request context.
items.recommendation: Include transactionHash in both individual and per-transaction block-replay envelopes. Do not require it for unsigned trace_call or trace_callMany simulations.
items.title: Replay transactionHash field

background: Parity's [trace-option mapping](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L36-L42) toggles transaction, VM and state tracers independently. Its [common response type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L646) always carries execution `output` and a trace vector, while VM and state components are optional. The [OpenEthereum `trace_call` example](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_call) shows empty bytes as `0x` and unrequested components as `null`; Parity's [mocked RPC test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/tests/mocked/traces.rs#L169-L177) confirms the stable envelope with an empty trace array.

The pinned [Erigon response type](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L81-L88) permits a nil trace slice, which serializes as `null` unless initialized. Nethermind's [replay writer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/ParityReplayEnvelopeWriter.cs#L14-L58) writes `output` from the trace object independently of the selected details; the observed stateDiff-only loss therefore needs tracing/data-flow investigation, not a different response schema.

background: Parity [added explicit trace errors in 2016](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/da2c2e5fc67010dbd6e6300d856b0dfa06f0b569). Its [failure enum](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/error.rs#L24-L95) maps VM failures to stable labels including Reverted and Out of gas; its [trace serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L501-L536) emits an `error` field on failure and omits `result`. Parity's [failure serialization test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L722-L743) locks this shape. The pinned [Nethermind writer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/ParityReplayEnvelopeWriter.cs#L94-L105) follows the same error-versus-result branch.

[EIP-140](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-140#specification) requires REVERT to retain returndata and unused gas for the caller, unlike an exceptional out-of-gas halt. That execution fact motivates preserving observed revert bytes and measured gas where a trace format can express them, but it does not itself define a failed-frame JSON `result`. The Besu and Nethermind cases should be separated into missing failure status, missing execution data, and wire-shape choices.

A failed-frame `result` is not new. Erigon and Reth have long emitted `result` on failed frames: `{gasUsed, output}` on a REVERT CALL and `result: null` on other failures ([Erigon trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L517-L529); revm-inspectors [types.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/blob/aac35449a4cacfe4c71477211a383c719acbf904/src/tracing/types.rs)), and Alloy and TrueBlocks decode both shapes. The new part is the failed-CREATE shape. Erigon and Reth report a reverted CREATE as `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address and the revert bytes under `code`; Alloy’s `TraceFilterMatcher` then matches that address against `toAddress`, where no contract exists. Besu and Nethermind emit `error` only. The envelope output cannot replace nested-frame revert bytes.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation required an explicit `result` on every failed frame, null when no data applied, and left the failure vocabulary undefined. Requiring null for an exceptional halt added nothing to `error` and forced Besu and Nethermind to change for no consumer benefit, so a halt may now omit `result`. The REVERT result stays required: Besu and Nethermind must add it, and Erigon and Reth must report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without the would-be address. The labels are Parity’s ([error.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/error.rs#L24-L95)) plus four post-Parity kinds. Only "Reverted" is universal today, so every client changes some labels: a static-context write is "Illegal state change" in Besu, "out of gas: write protection" in Erigon and the Geth draft, "Static call violation" in Nethermind and `StateChangeDuringStaticCall` in Reth; Erigon and the Geth draft lower-case "out of gas" and leak library text for precompile failures; Reth falls back to Rust `Debug` names such as `NotActivated`; Nethermind reports unknown failures as "Error" and precompile failures as "Out of gas". `revertReason` is emitted only by Besu, with raw bytes rather than decoded text. The frame gas rules were previously unwritten; every client already agrees with Parity on every frame in the matrix except Besu’s callMany frames (H16) and its degenerate `gasUsed` on raw and cross-fork filter paths. See [call-trace A1–A3 and A6](../../docs/source-review/call-trace.md).

### Settled details (2026-09-24, Geth implementation)

EIP-3860 defines an oversized CREATE initcode as an exceptional abort of the creating frame, treated like running out of gas, so that frame fails with "Out of gas" and no new label is needed. The designated invalid instruction 0xFE is an undefined opcode in Parity’s instruction table; its frame fails with "Bad instruction" (H20 omits the opcode from vmTrace).
items.next_step: Add discriminating fixtures: a mined reverted nested CREATE (also needed by H23), a static-context write, a precompile failure, an opcode not yet active and an SSTORE refund to pin root gasUsed before refunds. Compare labels exactly for the listed failure kinds, and assert root action.gas against the modelled intrinsic gas.
items.rationale: Consumers need the raw revert data and failure identity without parsing implementation-specific English or mistaking a failure for success. Only a REVERT carries data that error cannot; a null result on a halt adds nothing.
items.recommendation: The error field alone determines failure. A REVERT frame has error "Reverted" and requires result {gasUsed, output} with that frame’s gas and revert bytes, for CREATE too and never with address or code. An exceptional halt may omit result or set it to null; it consumes the frame’s action.gas. Use Parity’s failure labels: "Reverted", "Out of gas", "Bad instruction", "Bad jump destination", "Stack underflow", "Out of stack", "Mutable Call In Static Context", "Built-in failed" and "Out of bounds", plus "Contract address collision", "Code size limit exceeded", "Invalid code prefix 0xEF" and "Nonce overflow" for post-Parity failures. Any other string is an extension that consumers treat as a generic failure. revertReason, if present, is the decoded Error(string) text; raw revert bytes live in result.output. Frame gas follows Parity: root action.gas is the transaction gas minus intrinsic gas (including access-list and authorization costs); root result.gasUsed is execution gas before refunds, excluding intrinsic gas and the EIP-7623 floor; nested CALL-family action.gas is the gas forwarded after the 63/64 cap plus the 2300 stipend for a value transfer; CREATE gasUsed includes the code deposit.

background: Parity's [CreateResult type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L432-L450) has `gasUsed`, `code` and `address`; its [serializer test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L748-L769) expects those exact keys. The [executive tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L112-L125) fills `code` from the completed creation's deployed bytes; the action's `init` records constructor input. The [VM trace type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L109-L124) separately describes executing code.

Parity later [distinguished CREATE from CREATE2](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/87e108058125098ec404951393a054f08aebef7a) and [restored backward-compatible encoding](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/dcc6307f8a5f6037db6c99989d684985be9b8826). That history concerns creation-method metadata, not a change from `code` to `output`. The pinned [Besu flat-trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L330-L365) handles call output and creation code in adjacent branches, making the linked mixed-creation case important for checking where the published result gets its field name.

The zero-fee [constructor](../cases/initial/call-constructor.md) and [environment](../cases/coverage/model-environment-free.md) requests are H15 fee-validation probes. A fee-cap rejection has no creation result to assess, so H10 requires their priced counterparts instead. If a zero-fee request executes, the general creation-result assertion still checks its fields.

Parity emitted `creationMethod` ([trace.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L217-L229)). Erigon, Nethermind, Reth and the Geth draft emit it on every create frame in the evidence, and Alloy defaults it when absent. Besu emits it on 116 of 586 create frames and computes it per transaction: every create frame is labelled `create2` if any frame in the transaction executed CREATE2 ([FlatTraceGenerator.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L651-L666)). The `from`/`to`/`value` rules per call type are Parity’s ([trace.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/trace.rs#L225-L245)); all five implementations agree on them in the matrix.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous next step left creationMethod undecided and the action fields per call type unwritten. creationMethod is now required with the values `create` and `create2`, because CREATE2 changes address derivation and nothing else distinguishes the two. Only Besu moves. The call-type rules describe what every client already reports. See [call-trace A1 and A5](../../docs/source-review/call-trace.md).
items.next_step: Retain the successful mixed-creation probe and assert creationMethod on each frame, including a transaction that uses both CREATE and CREATE2. Add nested CALL and DELEGATECALL to an EIP-7702-delegated EOA, whose to is the EOA.
items.rationale: Creation has two different bytecodes—initcode and deployed code—and their field meanings should remain distinct.
items.recommendation: Use result.address, result.code and result.gasUsed for successful creation. result.code is deployed runtime bytecode, including "0x" for an empty deployment. Use result.output for CALL results; vmTrace.code for executing initcode. Every create action carries creationMethod, "create" or "create2", from the opcode that created that frame. CALL and STATICCALL report the caller as from and the target as to; DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE report the executing address as from and the code address as to. DELEGATECALL value is the inherited value and STATICCALL value is 0.

background: The [OpenEthereum trace guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_call) describes the requested trace types as an array containing one or more of `vmTrace`, `trace` and `stateDiff`. The [Parity RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L44-L58), however, used a plain vector; its [option mapping and call execution](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L36-L42) have no nonempty guard. With an empty vector all detail tracers are off, while the call still executes and yields its output. This is observed source behavior, not a documented promise.

The linked Nethermind case reaches an internal collection-reduction exception for an empty selection. That is independently a reporting bug. The proposed contract chooses to accept [] because output-only execution is useful and follows the same envelope rules as other selections; it intentionally clarifies the guide’s narrower “one or more” wording. A deliberate -32602 would be well formed but would still differ from this proposed selection policy.
items.next_step: A focused Nethermind fix and regression fixture can proceed independently of the broader API design.
items.rationale: An empty list of auxiliary views is a useful request for execution output alone. Its validity should not depend on whether detail tracers are enabled; fee-validation differences in the captured calls do not establish identical cross-client behavior.
items.recommendation: Accept an empty selection, execute the call and return its output with empty/unrequested components. Never leak a collection-reduction exception.

background: The [OpenEthereum guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_rawtransaction) documents only raw bytes and trace types. Parity's [RPC trait](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/traits/traces.rs#L55-L61) and [implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L169), however, accepted an optional third `BlockNumber`, defaulted omission to latest, and used the selected state and header. Explicit pending was rejected. The original published examples and source therefore disagree about whether the third argument was part of the public contract.

The pinned [Reth implementation](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L120-L141) likewise takes an optional block ID and selects its EVM environment; [Erigon](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/c25b8e47dc1a77ecdbd15d38ba3beae1d29530ec/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L1656), [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L141) and the Geth draft fork expose two parameters in the pinned source. Accepted third-argument syntax still requires an observable state-selection test, as the existing decision says.

The third selector is an inherited optional capability omitted from the old guide, not a newly invented Reth feature. The portable two-argument baseline reflects current client coverage while leaving that capability available. Adoption of a shared selector contract requires state-sensitive probes, not just accepted syntax. A historical selector means that block’s post-state; it is not necessarily the selected transaction’s pre-state, so it does not by itself make an already-mined signed transaction valid under H13.
items.next_step: Decide the extension contract with client teams. Keep extension requests and their results outside baseline assessment; preserve complete-response checks independently.
items.rationale: The baseline should be usable on all four today without silently changing which state is traced.
items.recommendation: Standardize the two-argument baseline with latest state. Observe an explicitly supplied third block selector as an extension, without marking its acceptance or rejection as baseline conformance. An accepted request alone does not prove that the selected state was used. Agree extension semantics and unsupported-argument errors separately.
items.title: Raw-transaction block argument

background: [Erigon supports strict execution validation](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890#issuecomment-5784143408), including balance and EIP-3607 sender-code checks. Error-code mapping and compatibility migration require client agreement.

Erigon reports that OpenEthereum skipped nonce checks and could supplement sender balance. Strict validation therefore changes legacy diagnostic behavior. A transaction pool can retain a future-nonce transaction that cannot execute next against the selected state. Block selectors conventionally refer to post-state; use transaction replay to obtain a mined transaction’s actual pre-transaction state.

The raw-validation corpus uses independently verified Prague state, funded controls and observable storage/output markers. It covers both nonce directions, chain identity, value and upfront-gas affordability, intrinsic gas, base fee and sender code, with valid EIP-7702 delegation and execution-OOG controls.

Erigon and Nethermind execute low- and high-nonce CREATE probes at the address derived from the state nonce. Constructor ADDRESS bytes, the returned address and created code in stateDiff agree. This establishes execution semantics without implying mutation of the signed bytes. Besu’s empty success-shaped results and Nethermind’s malformed responses are distinct from demonstrated execution. See the [H13 validation study](../../docs/h13-validation.md) for results and reproduction.

Parity's [raw RPC path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L170) used the same `client.call` as unsigned simulation. Its [virtual-call helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1206-L1233) explicitly disables nonce checking, while [`transact_virtual`](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L819-L833) supplies missing sender balance. The source comment identifies extra-block executions for consensus contracts and RPCs as the purpose of that virtual path. Thus permissiveness was a deliberate shared simulation mechanism in Parity; it is not evidence that modern clients silently rewrote signed bytes.

**Recommendation risk:** strict selected-state rejection gives a truthful execution-validity result but removes Parity's historical hypothetical-inspection behavior for future-nonce or underfunded signed transactions. The [Erigon review comment](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890#issuecomment-5784143408) supports strict execution; it does not by itself settle migration for callers relying on virtual simulation. Keep that compatibility question visible even though the validation direction is converged.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation proposed a single -32003 for every validation failure. `trace_rawTransaction` takes the same bytes as `eth_sendRawTransaction`, which already references the [#650](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/650) error-group catalog ([submit.yaml](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/465d1b98d43e94ff3d57e904fd7d4bea7f6b804c/src/eth/submit.yaml#L54-L59)). The revision reuses that catalog’s codes for nonce, gas, fee and funding rejections, so callers can tell them apart without matching text, and keeps -32003 as its generic fallback for failures without a group code, such as chain identity or sender code. Pool-only groups (already known, minimum price) do not apply. None of the tested builds emits the group codes on this method: Reth returns -32000 or -32003, Erigon -32000, and Besu and Nethermind return success-shaped or malformed responses, so all four need code changes. See [simulation §3](../../docs/source-review/simulation.md).
items.next_step: Agree the execution-validity requirements, the error-group mapping and a migration path for permissive diagnostic workflows. The raw-validation checks require each rejection to use its error-group code or the -32003 fallback and to name its violation. Keep H12 block-selection semantics separate.
items.rationale: A signed trace should describe those bytes executing against the selected state. Skipping nonce validation can change CREATE addresses and nonce-dependent behavior; overriding nonce or balance instead invents a different pre-state. Strict validation intentionally tightens historical permissive simulation and can reject queued or already-mined transactions at latest state. Client acceptance alone does not establish a deliberate nonce policy, and malformed error JSON does not prove validation was skipped.
items.recommendation: Validate trace_rawTransaction for execution against the selected state and fork: signature, chain identity, nonce equality (both low and high), balance for value and upfront gas, intrinsic gas, fees and sender-code restrictions with the EIP-7702 delegation exception. Do not change signed fields, override the sender nonce or supplement its balance. This is not pool admission: exclude local replacement, already-known and minimum-tip policies. Report a decodable transaction that fails validation with the eth_sendRawTransaction error groups: 1 nonce too low, 2 nonce too high, 800 intrinsic gas, 804 priority fee above fee cap, 806 fee cap below base fee and 809 insufficient funds, with -32003 (Transaction rejected) as the generic fallback; a signed gas limit above the server’s execution cap is rejected with -38026 rather than reduced; malformed encoding or parameters use -32602. Valid execution that REVERTs or halts still returns a trace.
items.title: Signed transaction execution validity

background: Parity's [RPC error helpers](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/errors.rs#L145-L178) distinguished invalid parameters from execution errors. The [raw trace handler](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L170) mapped invalid RLP through InvalidParams, while its [transaction-error helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/errors.rs#L466-L481) used a separate server code for transaction errors. [EIP-1474's error table](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#error-codes) later named `-32602` Invalid params and `-32003` Transaction rejected; aligning categories is better grounded than matching historical message text or Parity's private numeric transaction code.

Parity's [trace filter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L27-L46) and [call request](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/call_request.rs#L20-L42) rejected unknown fields. The draft deliberately accepts extra call-object fields for interoperability with shared transaction objects, while keeping filters closed. Fields the schema defines must take effect or be rejected, and conflicting fee fields are rejected. Ignoring extras cannot establish extension support and can hide typos; clients must declare supported extensions and callers must not infer support from success. H02 separately retains integer output paths and hex request indices.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation named no code for unsigned fee, funding or intrinsic-gas rejections, and the draft said unknown call-object fields MUST be ignored while treating standard fields as supported "when supported by the selected fork". Together these let a client that lacks a defined field run a different transaction and return a success-shaped trace. Erigon’s `TraceCallParam` declares only `data` among the calldata fields ([trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L66-L79)), so Go’s decoder drops `input`, `nonce`, `chainId`, `type`, `blobVersionedHashes` and `authorizationList`: a request using the canonical `input` field executes with empty calldata. Nethermind maps `data` into `input` so the last one wins, while Besu and Reth reject a mismatch; requiring agreement is stricter than Geth’s eth_call, which silently prefers `input`, and is a deliberate choice. The eth_simulateV1 codes are already emitted by Geth ([errors.go](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/internal/ethapi/errors.go#L103-L160)), Erigon, Nethermind and Reth from their eth_simulateV1 paths; Besu has no -380xx codes. Geth maps tip above cap to -32602 there, which the revision adopts. No corpus request sends `input` or any post-Berlin call field yet, so the Erigon defect is not captured. See [simulation §3, §12 and §13](../../docs/source-review/simulation.md).

### Settled details (2026-09-24, Geth implementation)

Implementing the codes in the Geth draft showed that three listed `eth_simulateV1` codes cannot occur for unsigned calls: a supplied nonce is neither validated nor used (H15), so -38010 and -38011 do not apply; a single call has no block of transactions to exceed (-38015); and unsigned calls skip the EIP-3607 sender-code check exactly as `eth_call` and `eth_simulateV1` do in Geth, so -38024 does not apply. Failures without a specific code, such as a blob fee cap below the blob base fee, a transaction type not active at the fork or an empty authorization list, use -32602 rather than an internal error. The [pinned draft](https://github.com/banteg/execution-apis/commit/53ffb857) states these codes.
items.next_step: Add a call-field corpus: input only, equal and disagreeing data/input, access list, authorization list, omitted from and gas, and a chainId mismatch. The fee and raw-validation checks accept the eth_simulateV1 codes and the error-group codes respectively.
items.rationale: Callers should distinguish a malformed request from a valid request that cannot execute, without text matching.
items.recommendation: Use -32602 for malformed encodings, wrong types, unsupported argument shapes, disagreeing data and input, a priority fee above the fee cap and a non-null override parameter a client does not implement. Report unsigned-call validation rejections with the eth_simulateV1 codes: -38012 base fee too low, -38013 intrinsic gas, -38014 insufficient funds, -38025 init-code size and -38026 client limit; a validation failure without a listed code is -32602. Report signed-transaction rejections with the eth_sendRawTransaction error groups (H13). List each method’s codes in its errors. Every call-object field the schema defines must take effect or cause a rejection; only fields outside the schema are ignored, and filters reject unknown fields. Keep messages implementation-specific; omit internal stack traces.
items.title: Invalid-parameter error codes

background: Parity's [call-request adapter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/helpers/fake_sign.rs#L24-L37) defaulted an unsigned call's `gasPrice` to zero and fake-signed it for the same [virtual execution path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1206-L1233) used by `trace_call` and `trace_callMany`. That path disabled nonce checks and used the requested block's header; it treated simulations as extra-block execution rather than pool admission. This explains the zero-fee precedent, but Parity predates `BASEFEE`. That is not precedent for preserving every environmental field: Parity's [call executors](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1490-L1538) also replaced the gas limit with U256::max_value(). The BASEFEE convention and preservation of the other selected block fields are explicit modern contract choices.

### Revised recommendation: zero-fee eth_call compatibility

The earlier H15 proposal preserved BASEFEE even for a zero-fee unsigned call. Reth’s compatibility objection changes this recommendation: adding tracing should not change the execution of the same call. Current upstream Geth `920c0777` explicitly zeroes BASEFEE in both [eth_call preparation](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/internal/ethapi/api.go#L794-L806) and [debug_traceCall preparation](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/eth/tracers/api.go#L948-L963) when the effective gas price is zero. This is an observable compatibility convention, not a claim that an unsigned simulator cannot technically preserve the header fee. Changing it should be coordinated across call methods. Reth’s zero-fee override is therefore no longer classified as an H15 environment defect; its positive-price validation and accounting are separate questions. Our Geth draft fork implements the earlier proposal and is not an independent upstream vote.

This is a revision to the proposed policy, not a statement of client-team agreement. The re-pinned draft at execution-apis e0e588fc states this rule, including the zero defaults below; its schema validates response structure, while the H15 semantic oracle checks behavior. The experimental Geth implementation still follows the earlier proposal. Neither is evidence of upstream consensus.

Reth's [unsigned-call environment](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/58a51b3ee3f6714ded9207b244a273c8afb592fd/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/helpers/call.rs#L882-L912) disables base-fee validation and fee charging, then sets the EVM block base fee to zero when the call's gas price is zero. Both [trace_call](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/58a51b3ee3f6714ded9207b244a273c8afb592fd/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L98-L109) and [trace_callMany](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/58a51b3ee3f6714ded9207b244a273c8afb592fd/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L149-L169) use this call setup. In the pinned [zero-fee](../cases/coverage/model-environment-free.md) probe, the tested release and development builds return GASPRICE 0 and BASEFEE 0 although the selected block's base fee is 765625000 wei. In the [priced](../cases/coverage/model-environment.md) probe, they return the supplied GASPRICE of 2 gwei and the original BASEFEE, but stateDiff shows no gas-fee debit. These are implementation observations, not client-team agreement; the dedicated fee-policy corpus also reads BASEFEE independently in single-call and mixed-fee callMany executions. Under the revised policy, the zero-fee BASEFEE result is expected. The disabled fee charging on valid priced requests remains a difference.

Besu’s trace methods use [transactionSimulator validation](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/f9572aa82a2dadb3dd1b218d3ca97101540faf97/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/AbstractTraceByBlock.java#L121-L123), which rejects underpriced execution; its processor [deducts gas upfront](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/f9572aa82a2dadb3dd1b218d3ca97101540faf97/ethereum/core/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/mainnet/MainnetTransactionProcessor.java#L254-L257) and [settles refunds and beneficiary rewards](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/f9572aa82a2dadb3dd1b218d3ca97101540faf97/ethereum/core/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/mainnet/MainnetTransactionProcessor.java#L530-L609).

Reth’s legacy/EIP-1559 distinction originates in its locked [alloy-evm 0.39.0 dependency](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/58a51b3ee3f6714ded9207b244a273c8afb592fd/Cargo.lock#L310-L313). Reth disables the later EVM base-fee check and gas-fee charging for unsigned calls.

Erigon instead [validates the fee cap](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/e26d9bd4056586e004488c31b561fb2663d46019/execution/protocol/txn_executor.go#L323-L329), while gasBailout [skips the sender debit](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/e26d9bd4056586e004488c31b561fb2663d46019/execution/protocol/txn_executor.go#L233-L247) without disabling the [beneficiary tip](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/e26d9bd4056586e004488c31b561fb2663d46019/execution/protocol/txn_executor.go#L750-L765). Fee validation and simulated payment therefore need separate assertions.

Omission and explicit zero are not interchangeable across clients. With all execution-fee fields omitted, [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/2a3b2531b4dcfaa58b21e4197c27cbab959a7f3e/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Facade/Eth/RpcTransaction/LegacyTransactionForRpc.cs#L110-L114), [Reth](https://github.com/alloy-rs/alloy-evm/blob/ba6f83b80aba8cf005175f4d776d8b90796c72d9/crates/evm/src/rpc/fees.rs#L92-L101) and the [Geth draft fork](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/internal/ethapi/transaction_args.go#L441-L455) default to zero; [Besu](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/f9572aa82a2dadb3dd1b218d3ca97101540faf97/ethereum/core/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/transaction/TransactionSimulator.java#L608-L617) and [Erigon](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/e26d9bd4056586e004488c31b561fb2663d46019/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L188-L211) default to the block base fee. An explicit maxFeePerGas 0 / maxPriorityFeePerGas 0 pair is accepted as zero-price execution by Nethermind, Reth and the Geth fork; Reth still changes BASEFEE to zero. Besu rejects the pair. Erigon replaces the pair with the block base fee and executes with GASPRICE = B. A zero priority fee alone is not a zero total fee.

The NoBaseFee name does not mean all fees are disabled. Upstream Geth skips fee validation only when [both execution-fee caps are zero](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/core/state_transition.go#L573-L589). Priced calls still enter [buyGas](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/core/state_transition.go#L435-L489), check cap-based funding, and debit the effective-price gas payment before EVM execution. [Settlement](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/920c07774c65ebb3023536f85df642c44478b540/core/state_transition.go#L761-L784) skips beneficiary payment for the all-zero exception and pays tips otherwise. Consequently, positive under-base-fee prices should still fail; a valid nonzero price requests ordinary simulated accounting. The zero-fee exception does not exempt value transfers from funding or disable gas metering.

For trace_callMany, start every item from the selected block environment and apply the zero-fee adjustment only to that item. A free → priced → free sequence sees BASEFEE 0 → B → 0, while balances and other simulated state carry forward. The existing fee-policy corpus checks this independently with both fee styles, mixed trace selections, upfront sender balance, prior beneficiary settlement, refunds, REVERT and out-of-gas. It must never carry a preceding call’s zeroed fee environment into a later priced call.

Its raw observations remain historical evidence. ### Paired checks and independent policy checks

The fee-compat corpus sends byte-for-byte identical call objects and block selectors through eth_call and every trace_call selection, including no trace components. Returned bytecode exposes seven words: GASPRICE, BASEFEE, NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, GASLIMIT, CALLER BALANCE after upfront payment/value, and COINBASE BALANCE before the tip. Each trace is assessed against an independently calculated policy output and separately compared with its own client’s eth_call result. Two identically wrong outputs therefore do not earn a policy pass. Rejections are compared by identifiable fee/funding reason, not error-message wording. Missing, malformed or generic/internal errors block the compatibility check. Omitted/incomplete fee defaults were observations under the previous recommendation; the revision below decides them.

Nethermind's malformed responses come from deferred trace execution: the writer starts a successful JSON-RPC envelope before fee/funding validation throws, so the request ID and closing brace are never written. The development capture has 232 such responses and 232 logged validation exceptions (128 base-fee, 104 funding). The [streaming investigation](../../docs/nethermind-streamed-errors.md) links the exact tested source, explains the release/development count difference, and identifies still-open [PR #13666](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/13666). Internal rejection is established by logs; valid RPC error delivery remains unverified in these responses.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation applied the zero-fee rule to explicit zero fees and left omitted and incomplete fee defaults, blob fees and overrides open. All nine tested eth_call builds agree that an omitted fee runs free (GASPRICE 0, BASEFEE 0, no debit), and eth_simulateV1’s `GenericCallTransaction` documents every fee default as 0 ([execute.yaml](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/465d1b98d43e94ff3d57e904fd7d4bea7f6b804c/src/schemas/execute.yaml#L240-L315)), so the principle H15 already applies decides them. The zero-fee condition moves from "explicit zero" to the effective price after defaulting, which is Geth’s rule ([transaction_args.go](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/internal/ethapi/transaction_args.go#L401-L495), [api.go](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/internal/ethapi/api.go#L798-L806)). The fee-validation skip stays a separate predicate (both caps zero); the two differ only for a zero cap with a positive tip, which is rejected anyway. The BLOBBASEFEE half of Geth’s rule is now explicit.

Compatibility cost: Besu and Erigon trace_call price an omitted fee at the base fee (Besu also charges it) while their eth_call runs free; Nethermind and the Geth draft keep BASEFEE at B for an omitted fee; Reth prices a tip-only request at B in both methods. Besu’s trace paths validate a supplied nonce ([AbstractTraceByBlock.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/AbstractTraceByBlock.java#L120-L123)), unlike its eth_call and every other client, and must ignore it instead. Erigon does not parse `nonce` at all. Enforcing funding removes Parity’s `transact_virtual` balance top-up for unsigned calls ([executive.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L821-L833)), a cost H13 already records for raw transactions. Overrides are already accepted in incompatible positions: Reth takes state and block overrides as parameters 4 and 5, Nethermind state overrides as parameter 4, Erigon a Geth-style config object as parameter 4, which silently ignores a Reth-style map; Besu takes none. Reserving the Reth positions with the eth_simulateV1 schemas moves Erigon. See [simulation §1, §7, §8, §14 and §15](../../docs/source-review/simulation.md).

### Settled details (2026-09-24, Geth implementation)

The Geth draft first rejected supplied gas above the RPC gas cap with -38026, reading "never truncate" literally. That made `trace_call` fail where the same `eth_call` succeeds, contrary to this decision’s premise that tracing must not change the call. Unsigned calls therefore run over-cap gas at the server cap, as `eth_call` does; the cap is server policy, not a truncated result. A signed raw transaction is different: capping its gas would change the signed transaction, so H13 rejects it with -38026. The [pinned draft](https://github.com/banteg/execution-apis/commit/53ffb857) states both rules.

items.rationale: Requesting a trace should not change the execution or fee semantics of an equivalent call. The zero-fee BASEFEE convention and zero defaults preserve established eth_call compatibility; they do not exempt positive prices from validation or payment. Enforcing funding removes Parity’s virtual balance top-up.
items.recommendation: Align unsigned trace simulations with eth_call and eth_simulateV1. Omitted fee fields default to 0. The zero-fee rule applies to the effective gas price after defaulting (gasPrice, or min(maxPriorityFeePerGas + base fee, maxFeePerGas)): a zero price runs with GASPRICE = 0, opcode-visible BASEFEE = 0 and no gas-fee balance effects. BLOBBASEFEE is 0 exactly when maxFeePerBlobGas is supplied as 0 or defaulted to 0 (it defaults to 0 when blobVersionedHashes are present); non-blob calls keep the real BLOBBASEFEE. Preserve the selected block’s other fields. Skip fee validation only when both fee caps are 0. Otherwise require the price to cover the base fee (-38012) and the priority-fee cap not to exceed the total cap (-32602), enforce funding (-38014), and simulate upfront gas payment, refunds, base-fee burn and beneficiary tips so execution and later calls observe them. A supplied nonce is accepted but neither validated nor used; CREATE addresses derive from the state nonce. gas is a uint64; omitted gas, and supplied gas above the server’s execution cap, run with that cap, as eth_call does. trace_call parameters 4 and 5 and trace_callMany parameters 3 and 4 are reserved for the eth_simulateV1 StateOverrides and BlockOverrides; a client that does not implement them rejects a non-null value with -32602, and with a block override the zero-fee rule uses the overridden base fee. Trace selections must not change execution. Apply the same rules independently to each trace_callMany item while carrying prior simulated state forward. Keep strict signed validation separate.

background: Parity's [multi-call executor](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1518-L1538) applies each call to one mutable state in order. Its [virtual-call helper](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1218-L1237) clones state immediately before a requested state diff, so each result describes that call relative to the preceding call's post-state. The [OpenEthereum multi-call guide](https://openethereum.github.io/JSONRPC-trace-module#trace_callmany) describes the same dependent-call purpose. This is stronger historical grounding than treating each result as an independent `trace_call` from the original block.

Parity's pre-1559 [transaction finalizer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L1160-L1175) refunded the sender and credited the block author with fees. [EIP-1559](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1559#specification) later split the effective gas price into a burned base fee and a beneficiary tip. Thus replay and signed raw traces should reflect the fork-correct actual state transition, while unsigned calls need the separate H15 fee policy. The pinned client state-diff sources and linked cases test the modern result; Parity alone cannot establish post-1559 accounting.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation said callMany diffs are sequential but not that each item is a separate transaction, what state the first item starts from, or how an item’s validation failure is reported, and its fee sentence omitted blob fees and fee collectors. All four clients already fail the whole request on an item error and reuse one header for every item, matching Parity and eth_simulateV1; only Erigon names the index, in message text. The new rules move Besu, whose `TraceCallMany` commits each call into a shared updater without marking a transaction boundary ([TraceCallMany.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceCallMany.java#L125-L142)), so a later call’s SSTORE uses the pre-bundle original value: its second `initial/call-many-priced` call uses 5,600 gas less than on every other build, and the reverted write in `a/many-storage-write-revert-read` 2,800 less. They also move Erigon’s historical trace_callMany, which reads a different state from trace_call (H28), and every client for the index in `error.data`. All nine builds already include the blob fee in the sender’s debit on `forks/replay-56`, and no transaction diff contains system-call, withdrawal or request-dequeue writes. See [statediff §1, §4, §8 and §9](../../docs/source-review/statediff.md) and [simulation §4](../../docs/source-review/simulation.md).

### Settled details (2026-09-24, Geth implementation)

A malformed item fails JSON-RPC parameter decoding before the method runs, so no implementation can attach an item index to it; the index requirement applies to decoded items that fail validation. The index is carried as `error.data.index`.

The accounting oracle includes blob fees and refunds; model fee collectors before assigning chains that use them.

items.recommendation: For signed/raw and mined replay, report the complete actual transition: the sender pays value, gasUsed times the effective gas price and blobGasUsed times the blob base fee; base and blob fees are burned or credited to a chain-defined collector; the tip goes to the fee recipient. For unsigned calls use H15’s policy. Block-level operations (system calls, withdrawals, rewards) belong to no transaction’s stateDiff, so concatenated diffs do not reconstruct the block post-state. In trace_callMany every item is a separate transaction: EIP-2200/3529 original storage values, EIP-2929 access sets, EIP-1153 transient storage, the refund counter and the EIP-6780 same-transaction scope start afresh, while all items share one block environment (NUMBER and TIMESTAMP do not advance). The first item runs against the same state and environment as trace_call at the selected block. Each result describes its own transition from the preceding item’s post-state; reverted EVM writes roll back, while fork-defined transaction-level nonce and fee effects survive. If any decoded item fails validation, return one error with the zero-based item index in error.data.index and no partial results; a malformed item is invalid params (-32602) without an index. A server may cap items or total gas only with an explicit -38026 error, never by truncating.

background: Parity's [account diff algorithm](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L134) compares optional account existence before comparing fields: absent-to-present marks balance, nonce, code and present storage as Born; present-to-absent marks them Died; present-to-present uses Same or Changed. Its [RPC serializer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L160-L207) encodes those variants as `+`, `-`, `=` and `*`. The [original create/delete test](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/state.rs#L88-L114) explicitly expects a newly created account's zero nonce and empty code to be `+`.

This history explains why `+` is an existence marker, not shorthand for a nonzero or nonempty value. A pre-existing empty-code account is therefore a changed or unchanged account, not a birth. Nethermind `StateProvider.ReportChanges` suppresses the code callback when both byte lengths are zero, collapsing absent code and existing empty code. Its release Parity converter then writes `=` for an unreported code change. PR #13668 reconstructs the empty-code marker from balance existence. The [source audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md#why-the-code-produces-these-results) links each pinned implementation.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation defined account markers but not account inclusion or slot markers. The Geth draft reports zero-to-value and value-to-zero slots on a surviving account as `+` and `-` ([trace_capture.go](https://github.com/banteg/go-ethereum/blob/fa8ecb9242dda61858c44cf43c70d00548fbd7cd/eth/tracers/trace_capture.go#L245-L251)), while Parity, Besu, Erigon, Nethermind and Reth all report `*` from or to the zero word; the harness accepted both until [fb511d3c](https://github.com/banteg/trace-interop/commit/fb511d3c) and now rejects the Geth form. Parity never used `=` for a slot ([account_diff.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/types/src/account_diff.rs#L64)), and the schema no longer allows it. A born account lists only nonzero slots in Besu, Erigon, Reth and Geth; Parity could leak a zero `+` for a slot written and then cleared. An existing EIP-161-empty account removed by touch-clearing splits clients three ways (Besu and Erigon report `-`, Nethermind a schema-invalid `*` to null, Reth and the Geth draft omit it), but such accounts cannot be created after Spurious Dragon and no fixture has one. On the captured cases only the Geth draft moves. See [statediff §2 and §5](../../docs/source-review/statediff.md).

items.rationale: Absent accounts and existing accounts with empty code are different states; consumers should be able to reconstruct the change without guessing. Reserving + and - for account birth and death keeps a slot marker from implying an existence change.
items.recommendation: Make account existence explicit. An account appears only if its balance, nonce, code, storage or existence changed; existence means presence in the state trie, so an existing EIP-161-empty account removed by touch-clearing is a deletion. + and - appear only when the account is born or dies: a born account marks balance, nonce (including zero) and code (including empty) with +, and lists its nonzero post-state slots as +. For an account that exists at both endpoints, unchanged fields use =, changed fields use *, and changed slots always use * with 32-byte from/to words, including zero words; slots never use =. If an address already existed with empty code, do not mark it as newly created. Compare existence at the execution endpoints; transient creation and destruction with an account absent at both endpoints does not produce an account diff.
