background: Parity's [state-diff algorithm](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L136) compares account code in the pre- and post-state independently of trace actions. That predates EIP-7702 but supplies the right historical meaning of `stateDiff.code`: changed existing code uses `*`, new-account code uses `+`, and deletion uses `-`. The pinned [Reth state-diff path](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs) and linked authorization cases show an implementation can miss code written during transaction preprocessing even when later EVM execution is traced.

[EIP-7702](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702#behavior) writes a delegation indicator or clears code while processing authorizations before the execution portion. It explicitly preserves processed authorizations even if the later execution reverts. The EIP's rationale explains why delegation was made persistent. A complete transaction state diff therefore has to include the authorization-side code change despite a failed call frame.

EIP-7702 permits multiple valid tuples from one authority, with the last valid code write winning. stateDiff reports their net effect, not each intermediate write. Authorization processing also skips certain invalid tuples without rejecting an otherwise valid outer transaction; H13’s execution-validity rule must follow those fork-defined distinctions. Event-level authorization history would require a separate output contract.

[revm-inspectors #509](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/pull/509), which compares EIP-7702 code hashes when building state diffs ([parity.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/blob/aac35449a4cacfe4c71477211a383c719acbf904/src/tracing/builder/parity.rs)), has merged into main but is unreleased after 0.43.0, which Reth main still locks. The Reth rows change only after a release and a Reth dependency bump.
items.next_step: Fix net account code-change reporting and add multiple-authorizations probes, including a final code value equal to the pre-state. Distinguish invalid outer transactions from authorization tuples skipped under EIP-7702.
items.rationale: stateDiff must include code that changed, even if the account already existed.
items.recommendation: Report net pre/post delegation-code changes, including set, replace and clear, independently of account-creation flags. Preserve authorization effects when later execution reverts. Multiple accepted authorizations that restore the original code produce no net code change, although nonce changes may remain.

background: Parity's [VM tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L277-L296) stores the `code` bytes passed when an execution subtrace begins, and the [executor](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L953-L966) passes the chosen action's code, not a later address lookup. This explains the original `vmTrace.code` field as executing bytecode. For CREATE that is initcode, while H10's `result.code` is deployed runtime code.

[EIP-7702](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702#delegation-indicator) adds delegation-code resolution after Parity's era: execution follows one indicated target and stops after that first hop, while external code-reading opcodes inspect the indicator itself. The trace therefore needs the resolved executed bytes in a delegated frame, not the authority's 23-byte indicator or a stale pre-state lookup. The pinned [Reth trace builder](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs) and [inspector dependency](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/blob/453c67d7ccdf51327c9e7687ac6ba0b8651e7f87/src/tracing/builder/parity.rs) are the relevant modern path for the linked missing-initcode case.
items.next_step: Fix bytecode population separately from the already-retested instruction deltas. Add EIP-7702 one-hop controls: a delegation target that itself delegates must not be followed recursively, and delegation to a precompile executes empty code rather than the native precompile.
items.rationale: The operations must be decodable against the bytes in their own frame.
items.recommendation: Record the bytecode actually executed in each frame: initcode for creation, resolved implementation code for delegation, and the relevant code source for delegatecall/callcode. Do not populate it from an address-only pre-state lookup after tracing.

background: Parity's [interpreter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L348-L405) calls the VM tracer before an opcode with its cost and reported memory region, then after the opcode with the current remaining gas, pushed stack words and memory. The [VM tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L241-L274) stores that after-step gas in the value serialized as `ex.used` and extracts that post-step memory slice. Its internal field is named `gas_used`, but the passed value is remaining gas; the recommendation follows the execution path rather than the misleading name.

[EIP-5656](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5656#semantics) introduced MCOPY after Parity's codebase and defines it as an actual destination-memory write, including overlapping copies. Erigon handles MCOPY's destination ([trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L593-L596)): development build e26d9bd4 reports it on `a/call-mcopy` and `coverage/model-mcopy-overlap`, and only release 3.6.1 misses it. The pinned [Besu VM generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/vm/VmTraceGenerator.java) still omits it.

Parity's [memory-region calculation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L472-L493) included MLOAD and the entire requested CALL output window. Those were post-step snapshots of the operand range, not exclusively writes. Erigon ([trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L593-L596)), Nethermind and Besu ([VmTraceGenerator.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/vm/VmTraceGenerator.java#L235)) all still report MLOAD this way. For the CALL output window there is no majority: Parity and Erigon report the full window; the Geth draft and revm-inspectors main report the returned bytes; Besu reports the returned bytes or a value copied from the calling frame’s final RETURN ([VmTraceGenerator.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/vm/VmTraceGenerator.java#L314-L324)); Nethermind reports nothing.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation narrowed `mem` to bytes actually written, which gave MLOAD no memory delta and trimmed a short CALL return, and deferred the call/return gas boundary and failed-operation conventions to fixtures. The narrowing departed from Parity and from all three established implementations for MLOAD; on the dedicated model cases it was the only H20 difference for Erigon e26d9bd4 and Nethermind 641592d2. The revision reverses it. Erigon, Nethermind and Besu now conform on MLOAD, while our Geth draft fork and unreleased revm-inspectors main, which followed the narrowing, must change. For the CALL output window Erigon already conforms; Nethermind, Besu, the Geth draft and revm-inspectors main change.

The gas, halt and step rules are Parity’s ([mod.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L336-L415)) and most clients already follow them; on the replay-tree root CALL, Erigon, Nethermind and the Geth draft all report cost 71,624 and used 569,571. They move: Besu (stipend in value-CALL cost, precompile execution cost instead of forwarded gas, and cost = all remaining gas with used 0 for a failed operation); the Geth draft and Nethermind (CREATE cost without forwarded gas; Nethermind’s streaming tracer loses its base tracer’s addition); Erigon (keeps `ex`, and even `store`, for a failed static SSTORE) and Nethermind (deletes most failed operations); the synthetic STOP emitted by Erigon, the Geth draft and Reth; Nethermind’s DUPn `push` (n words, captured before the copy) and Besu’s top-first multi-word `push` (source only); Nethermind’s `store` (present only when stateDiff is also selected); revm-inspectors main’s `store` (set on a cold SLOAD and missing on a warm unchanged SSTORE; Reth 0.43.0 never sets it); the Geth draft’s null vmTrace for an EOA target and null `sub` for precompile and empty-code targets (also revm-inspectors main); and Erigon’s extra `sub` on SELFDESTRUCT and on calls that fail their precheck. See [vmtrace A1–A6, B6 and C1–C8](../../docs/source-review/vmtrace.md).

Add fixtures that exercise them: DUP/SWAP push with distinct values, a vmTrace SSTORE fixture (warm unchanged write, cold read), code that runs off its end, a short CALL return over a nonzero tail, and EOA, precompile and empty-code targets.
items.rationale: Same-step effects let consumers follow execution without shifting writes between opcodes. An operand-derived range needs no return-data dependency and is exactly what Parity and three established clients report; a consumer that applies mem as a write reconstructs memory under either rule. The gas and halt rules make the nested-gas relation used = previous used − cost + child leftover checkable without opcode knowledge.
items.recommendation: mem is the post-operation contents of the memory range the opcode’s operands designate: MSTORE and MLOAD [off, off+32), MSTORE8 [off, off+1), the destination of CALLDATACOPY, CODECOPY, EXTCODECOPY, RETURNDATACOPY and MCOPY, and the full CALL-family output window. It is null when that range is empty or the opcode designates none (RETURN, REVERT, LOG*, KECCAK256, CREATE*). cost is the total gas deducted from the caller when the operation starts, including gas made available to a child frame (CALL family: the 63/64-capped forwarded gas, excluding the value stipend; CREATE family: all but 1/64). ex.used is the caller’s remaining gas after the operation, including unused child gas returned. An operation that began executing and halted exceptionally is present with its pre-execution cost, ex: null and sub: null; operations rejected before execution (undefined opcodes including the designated invalid 0xFE, stack underflow or overflow) are omitted, and there is no synthetic STOP, so every pc lies inside code. push is the top k stack words after execution, deepest first, where k is the number of words the opcode leaves in place of its inputs (DUPn and SWAPn n+1, CALL and CREATE 1 after the child returns). store is set only by SSTORE, from its key and value operands as quantities, whenever the SSTORE completes, even if the value is unchanged; TSTORE and SLOAD never set it. A selected vmTrace is always an object. An operation that entered a child frame, including precompile and empty-code targets, has that frame’s trace as sub ({code: "0x", ops: []} if no instruction ran); operations that entered no frame (failed precheck, SELFDESTRUCT) have sub: null.

background: Parity's [VM operation type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L43-L124) serializes pushed stack items as `U256` quantities, but code and memory deltas as byte data. Its original operation record has `pc`, `cost`, `ex` and `sub`; it does not require mnemonic `op` or sequence `idx` fields. [EIP-1474's encoding rules](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474#value-encoding) distinguish minimal `Quantity` values such as `0x0` from even-length `Data` bytes such as `0x00`, which explains the recommendation's different encodings.

The pinned [Nethermind VM serializer](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Blockchain/Tracing/ParityStyle/ParityVmOperationTraceConverter.cs#L40-L67) serializes its stored `Push` items directly; the linked cases show padded words. Adding `op` or `idx` can help tools display a trace, but the original Parity record did not need them to reproduce execution. Their presence should therefore be checked for consistency without making older traces invalid.

background: Parity's [executive tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L106) records a root precompile as a call frame and writes the actual bytes passed to `done_trace_call` into that frame's `result.output`. The separate [execution envelope](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace.rs#L625-L646) carries `output` from the completed execution even when no VM bytecode operations exist. Thus the two output locations refer to the same return bytes for a successful root call; the absence of EVM code is not a reason to empty either one.

The pinned [Besu flat-trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L70-L125) special-cases a precompiled gas cost while constructing the root frame. The linked identity-precompile case is a direct discriminator: an execution envelope with correct return bytes does not prove the corresponding frame's result was populated. H29 separately decides which nested precompile frames exist.

items.recommendation: Report actual return bytes in each successful call-frame result, including precompiles with no EVM bytecode. The execution envelope output must equal the successful root call’s output; nested calls can return different bytes.

background: Parity's [original address matcher](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L82-L110) assigns sender/recipient equivalents per action: CREATE uses the creator and successful result address, SELFDESTRUCT uses the destroyed account and refund address, and PoW reward uses its author as the recipient. This mapping is part of the indexed filter implementation, not a reinterpretation of a generic `to` field. The pinned Besu CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT cases test that the same records visible in `trace_block` can be found by their relevant addresses.

[Parity issue #9822](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/issues/9822) reported that `trace_filter` dropped a failed contract creation visible by transaction/block tracing; [the fix](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/1ac1224cd3f983d66d650e78428d274350c84a30) addressed that historical edge. a failed CREATE has no successful `result.address`. Parity's matcher still allows a creator-only query to find it but cannot satisfy a nonempty recipient filter. The proposed mapping preserves that distinction instead of assigning a successful destination to a failed creation.

Reward and failed-CREATE matching diverge in source, and no fixture covers them yet. Besu filters rewards through the generic `action.getFrom()` and `action.getTo()` ([TraceFlatTransactionStep.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceFlatTransactionStep.java#L61-L80)) and Nethermind through `action.From` and `action.To` ([TxTraceFilter.cs](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/ac02224f25fd4901116ebf2643d522ec4a0e60a1/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TxTraceFilter.cs#L41-L57)); a reward action carries only `author`, so `toAddress: [miner]` never returns rewards in either client. Erigon emits a reward whenever the coinbase is in `toAddress` ([trace_filtering.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_filtering.go#L597-L617)), ignoring `mode` and `fromAddress`, so an intersection with a populated sender list still returns it. Nethermind sets a failed CREATE’s `action.To` to the would-be address ([ParityLikeTxTracer.cs](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/ac02224f25fd4901116ebf2643d522ec4a0e60a1/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Blockchain/Tracing/ParityStyle/ParityLikeTxTracer.cs#L413-L421)) and matches on it; Reth’s Alloy matcher uses a failed CREATE’s `result.address`, which Reth and Erigon still report (H09). Reth and the Geth draft otherwise match the draft.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous wording called the SELFDESTRUCT side the "destroyed account", which is inaccurate after EIP-6780, when the account usually survives, and did not spell out reward matching under each mode. The matching itself is unchanged and follows Parity ([filter.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/types/filter.rs#L96-L121)). Writing the reward rule down exposes Besu and Nethermind (rewards unreachable through `toAddress`) and Erigon (rewards ignore `mode`). See [filter-selection §2, §5 and §11](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md).
items.next_step: Add reward fixtures on the PoW `forks` chain (toAddress set to the coinbase, and an intersection with a sender list) and a mined reverted CREATE queried by its would-be address and by its creator. The filter oracles already ignore a failed CREATE’s result address.
items.rationale: Address-based history should not silently omit a transfer or creation because its action uses different field names.
items.recommendation: Define from/to equivalents per action: creator and successfully created address for CREATE; the executing (self-destructing) account and beneficiary for SELFDESTRUCT, which after EIP-6780 usually survives; and recipient only for rewards. A failed CREATE has no created-address match: it can match its creator, but not a populated recipient list. A reward matches toAddress by author and has no from side: in intersection mode it is excluded whenever fromAddress is populated, while in union mode a toAddress match suffices. Apply H03 composition, so union can retain a creator match. Matching a reverted action does not imply a committed transfer.

background: Parity's [original flat tracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L151) pushes a frame index on entry, then writes either its result or its failure to that exact frame when the EVM exits it. Its child count and traceAddress advance independently of the outcome. This is the historical reason to attach an error to a call frame rather than infer it from another frame's opcode stream: an EVM caller can inspect a failed CALL's success bit and then return successfully.

In the pinned [Besu flat trace generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L549-L565), `hasRevertInSubCall` scans the transaction-wide trace frames for a matching depth, without first delimiting the current call's subtree. It is used when assigning the root and nested frame errors. That explains why the sibling fixtures can report a handled revert on the wrong frame; the observed trace result remains the regression oracle for this diagnosis.
items.next_step: Prepare a focused Besu regression and fix without waiting for broad schema policy.
items.rationale: A successful caller can handle a failed subcall and continue; frame results must preserve that distinction.
items.recommendation: Attach error and result data to the actual call frame. A sibling failure must not change another frame's status. A child’s local success remains success even if a later ancestor revert rolls back its state changes; frame outcome and committed stateDiff answer different questions.
items.title: Sibling failure isolation

background: Parity's [original `trace_rawTransaction` implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L148-L168) parses RLP, validates the signed transaction and resolves the state/header before returning a `Result<TraceResults>`; each failure maps to an RPC error instead of a partial trace object. The later [Ethereum RPC error specification](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474) likewise describes an `error` member on the response object, so this decision concerns response integrity independently of which signed transactions a client accepts.

The pinned [Nethermind trace module](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L141-L177) validates RLP before tracing but, when streaming is enabled, `BuildStreamingSingleResult` returns a lazy streaming result whose execution runs while the JSON writer is active. This makes a late admission or execution failure a different problem from malformed RLP. prevalidating the request alone cannot ensure a complete JSON-RPC error if a deferred trace fails after result bytes have been sent; buffering or an error-safe streaming boundary is needed for that guarantee. An explicit transport abort is an incomplete request, not a successful trace or a complete JSON-RPC error; it cannot count as passing the semantic assessment.
items.next_step: Retain raw malformed-response evidence. Test both pre-commit JSON-RPC errors and post-commit failures through the actual transport, including later callMany validation and cancellation; distinguish explicit transport aborts from malformed completed responses.
items.rationale: Clients must be able to parse failures and associate them with a request, regardless of the chosen signed-transaction admission policy.
items.recommendation: Before committing result bytes, report validation or execution setup failures as one complete JSON-RPC error. Buffer when necessary to guarantee a replaceable response. After output has been committed, a later failure must explicitly abort the transport rather than append a second envelope or finish a partial result as success. Request parsing alone is not full validation; later callMany admission can depend on earlier calls.
items.title: Well-formed errors for rejected raw transactions

background: Parity's [original account diff](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/pod/src/account.rs#L103-L140) distinguishes a present account becoming absent (`Died` for balance, nonce, code and each prior storage slot supplied to that helper; in practice none were, see below) from an account that remains present with changed values. Its [transaction finalizer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/machine/src/executive.rs#L1132-L1181) actually removed SELFDESTRUCT accounts at the end of execution under those pre-Cancun rules. The deletion markers therefore describe account existence, not merely a zeroed balance.

[EIP-6780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6780) deliberately changed that premise: SELFDESTRUCT normally transfers the balance without deleting a pre-existing account's code or storage, preserving deletion only for a contract created in the same transaction. This explains why the selected block's fork rules determine the stateDiff, and why the Nethermind/Reth pre-Cancun missing code and nonce markers are meaningful. `stateDiff` compares the before and after account snapshots. A contract created and destroyed within the same transaction can leave no account at either endpoint, so even genuine transient deletion need not produce a `Died` entry; an execution trace is needed to see that event. A prefunded address, however, existed before creation; deletion at that address can require a net deletion entry.

Parity in fact emitted `storage: {}` for a deleted account. [Account::to_pod](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/account-state/src/account.rs#L142-L157) exposes only `storage_changes`, and [state diff construction](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/account-state/src/state.rs#L868-L926) takes a killed account’s keys from the pre-state clone’s dirty changes plus the queried account, which is `None` after deletion and short-circuits. The pre-state clone is clean for `trace_call` and for a replay’s first transaction, so no slot reached the `Died` helper; only keys dirtied by earlier uncommitted calls in the same bundle or block could appear, which is a quirk. Besu ([StateTraceGenerator.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/diff/StateTraceGenerator.java#L142)) and Erigon also report `{}`; Nethermind reports written slots as `*` to zero, the Geth draft written slots as `-`, and revm-inspectors main accessed nonzero slots as `-`.

Reth’s missing deletion markers are fixed upstream by [revm-inspectors #510](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/pull/510), merged into main but unreleased after 0.43.0, which Reth main still locks. Nethermind release 2.0.0 reports a pre-Cancun deletion as `*` to `null` for balance, nonce and code, which is schema-invalid rather than merely missing markers; the harness checks only code and nonce.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation left the enumeration of untouched prior slots open. The revision adopts `storage: {}`, which is deterministic, cheap, and what Parity, Besu and Erigon already report. It moves Nethermind (written slots as `*` to zero), the Geth draft (written slots as `-`) and revm-inspectors main (accessed nonzero slots as `-`). The current fixture account has no storage, so none of these differences is captured yet. See [statediff §6 and §11](../../docs/source-review/statediff.md).
items.next_step: Retain deletion-marker regressions. Give the deleted fixture account nonzero storage, and add same-transaction creation and destruction at an absent and a prefunded address.
items.rationale: Deletion and a zero balance with retained code are observably different states. Apply the rules of the selected block.
items.recommendation: Compare account existence before and after the execution. For present-to-absent accounts, use deletion markers for balance, nonce and code, and report storage: {}; the account’s - implies that all storage is wiped, so no slot is listed. After EIP-6780 a pre-existing contract normally survives SELFDESTRUCT, so do not report code deletion. An account absent at both endpoints has no net account diff, even if created and destroyed during execution.
items.title: Account deletion across Cancun

background: Parity's [original trace database filter](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L349-L365) searched indexed trace blooms over the requested range, loaded each stored block's traces, and filtered those records. The trace namespace thus established per-block result consistency without requiring a range request to execute blocks again. This matters across forks because each stored trace was produced with the rules in force when its block was imported.

The pinned [Besu range pipeline](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceFilter.java#L142-L202) obtains one `protocolSpec` and transaction processor from its first block header, then feeds a list of blocks to the pipeline. That is a plausible cause of the reproduced difference between a cross-fork filter and the same individual block traces; the fixture comparison, rather than code inspection alone, establishes the defect. The requirement is output equivalence and fork-correct provenance, not a mandate to re-execute indexed traces.

Besu’s range execution skips more than fork rules. `TraceFilterSource` streams every block’s transactions into one `ChainUpdater` ([TraceFilterSource.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceFilterSource.java#L40-L55), [TraceBlock.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/TraceBlock.java#L192-L216)), and `ExecuteTransactionStep` processes transactions only ([ExecuteTransactionStep.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/ExecuteTransactionStep.java#L84-L111)). Between blocks no block reward, withdrawal, beacon-root, history or request processing is applied, so block N+1 executes on block N’s post-transaction state rather than its post-block state. Besu’s `trace_block` and `trace_filter` also never run the pre-execution system calls, although its `debug_traceBlock` does, so a transaction that reads the EIP-4788 or EIP-2935 contracts is traced against stale system storage even in a single-block query (H28).

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous client-facing change said only "use each block’s own execution rules", which invites a fix that swaps the protocol spec per block and leaves the state skew in place. The recommendation now names the starting state and the pre-transaction system operations. It still moves only Besu. See [filter-selection §7](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md).
items.next_step: The repeated fixtures are ready for a focused processor-context investigation and regression. Add a range whose later block spends a withdrawal credited in the earlier block, which exposes the state skew independently of fork rules.
items.rationale: The same block must not trace differently depending on the other blocks included in a query.
items.recommendation: Return records produced with each block’s own fork rules and state, whether retrieved from an index or replayed: each block is traced from its parent’s post-block state with its own pre-transaction system operations applied, under its own fork rules. Filtering and pagination over the ordered range must agree with the corresponding per-block records. Do not reuse one block’s execution rules, or its post-transaction state, across a block boundary.
items.title: Filter execution across fork boundaries

background: Parity's [original replay path](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/src/client/client.rs#L1639-L1667) obtained `state_at_beginning(block)` from the parent block's post-state, then applied the selected block's transactions in order with its own environment. That is the lineage for distinguishing replay's pre-block starting state from the post-state used by a historical simulated call. Parity predates the current beacon-root and block-hash system writes, so its transaction-only loop is not a complete modern replay recipe.

[EIP-4788](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788) and [EIP-2935](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2935) perform their system updates at the start of the selected block, before transactions. Consequently, block N's post-state includes those writes and block N+1's does not belong in a query at N. Erigon [PR #24056](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/24056), merged on 2026-09-18 as [66571d04390](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/commit/66571d043907723f190fbe1f882008c27008fa29), identified a history reader opened one transaction index too late: Min(N+1)+1 included the next block's system call. It changes the historical trace_call, debug_traceCall and default-index debug_traceCallMany readers from txnIndex 0 to -1 and adds TestTraceCallExcludesNextBlockSystemCall. The maintainer explicitly retained 0 for trace_callMany because that method selects the parent block. The captured v3.6.1 release predates the fix; development c25b8e47 contains it and passes the H28 checks.

The H28 probes use `trace_call` and `eth_getStorageAt` only, so they do not exercise replay. Besu opens the parent world state ([Tracer.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/processor/Tracer.java#L42-L53)) and then processes the block’s transactions without its pre-execution system calls ([ExecuteTransactionStep.java](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/07f0a4b2f832257842db71eacf4bca584f87fafe/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/methods/ExecuteTransactionStep.java#L84-L111)); only its plugin `TraceServiceImpl` runs them. A mined transaction that reads the EIP-4788 contract at its own timestamp, or the EIP-2935 slot for its parent, therefore sees stale storage in Besu replay. The open [Besu #10953](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/10953) replays block pre-execution before tracing transactions.

The maintainer’s reason for keeping txIndex 0 in `trace_callMany` does not hold. That method executes with block N’s header and base fee but reads state after N+1’s pre-block system transaction ([trace_adhoc.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/jsonrpc/trace_adhoc.go#L1347), [helper.go](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/3b4861d10387ca3e19f7b16d1b8c0ec1fcd616cd/rpc/rpchelper/helper.go#L175-L190)), so its first item sees N+1’s beacon-root and history writes while `trace_call` at N does not. Parity’s `call_many` used the same state and header as `call`, and Erigon’s own `debug_traceCallMany` default moved to −1. Not yet verified at runtime.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation did not say that `trace_call` and the first `trace_callMany` item share one state, nor that replay applies the block’s own pre-transaction system operations. Both are now explicit (H16, H27). They move Besu replay and Erigon’s historical `trace_callMany`, neither of which the current probes capture. See [statediff §3 and §4](../../docs/source-review/statediff.md).

Add a mined transaction that reads the EIP-4788 contract at its own timestamp and replay it with stateDiff (Besu), and a trace_callMany twin of the historical beacon-root call (Erigon). The current H28 probes use trace_call and eth_getStorageAt only; unrelated H09 schema failures still block the stricter harmonization milestone.
items.rationale: A future system write must not appear in an earlier block's state. This is an execution-context issue, not a cosmetic trace encoding choice.
items.recommendation: Historical state at block N should include that block’s changes, including system operations, but none from N+1. Replay starts from the parent’s post-block state, applies the block’s pre-transaction system operations once, then its preceding transactions. trace_call and the first trace_callMany item at block N run against the same state and environment.

background: Parity's [original ExecutiveTracer](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L41-L108) explicitly skipped only a non-root built-in call whose `ActionParams.value.value()` was zero. It incremented the parent's subtrace count and path only for retained frames; its success and failure callbacks both cleared the skip flag for an omitted built-in. That is the trace namespace's historical frame policy, rather than a consequence of whether the precompile did useful computation or succeeded.

The old [ActionValue definition](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/vm/src/action_params.rs#L29-L62) makes `value()` return either a transferred or an apparent value. A DELEGATECALL can therefore retain a frame because it inherits a nonzero apparent value even though it moves no funds. The pinned [Besu generator](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/blob/d997aad7b3be6333464c0687d3761c568ee63524/ethereum/api/src/main/java/org/hyperledger/besu/ethereum/api/jsonrpc/internal/results/tracing/flat/FlatTraceGenerator.java#L280-L313) skips precompile calls during frame construction; the crossed outer/child value fixtures isolate the incompatibility. This inherited-value exception is a historical compatibility rule, not a value-transfer assertion.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation did not say which precompile set applies, or whether calls that fail their precheck emit frames. Parity’s builtin check is fork-aware ([executive_tracer.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/executive_tracer.rs#L44)), as are revm-inspectors and Erigon. Clients split 3/3 on prechecks: Parity ([mod.rs](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/evm/src/interpreter/mod.rs#L633-L637)), Besu and Nethermind emit no frame for a CALL that fails the depth or balance check, while Erigon, the Geth draft and Reth emit one with an error. Parity reported a CREATE collision as "Out of gas"; Nethermind emits no collision frame. Following Parity moves Erigon, the Geth draft and Reth for prechecks (Geth and Erigon already drop CREATE precheck frames from Amsterdam) and Nethermind for collisions. No fixture covers depth, nested insufficient balance or collisions yet. See [call-trace A4 and A8](../../docs/source-review/call-trace.md).
items.next_step: Review the inherited DELEGATECALL exception as a compatibility choice. Add a zero-value call to 0x0a before Cancun and to 0x100 before Osaka, a depth bomb, a nested value CALL beyond balance and a CREATE2 collision. The precompile-values corpus separates outer and child values, pre-funds zero-value creations with a preceding simulated transfer, and returns the call success bit. Parent error propagation remains a separate H24 issue.
items.rationale: The retained inherited-value exception is a compatibility choice, not a statement that DELEGATECALL transfers funds. Crossed-value CALL/CALLCODE fixtures confirm that Erigon, Reth and Nethermind use the explicit child value rather than the outer value. Besu still omits the nonzero-value child. The independent Geth draft implementation also matches these checks; it is not an independent vote for the policy.
items.recommendation: Retain root precompile calls. Omit nested precompile frames with zero value; retain those with nonzero transferred or inherited value, whether successful or failed. A precompile is an address in the precompile set active at the executing block’s fork, so a zero-value call to an address before its precompile activates is an ordinary call and keeps its frame. A CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck (depth limit, insufficient balance) starts no execution and emits no frame; a CREATE address collision emits a create frame with error "Contract address collision" that consumes its gas. Number traceAddress and subtraces over the emitted tree. Keep caller VM return-memory effects even when a child frame is omitted.
items.title: Precompile call-frame inclusion

background: The pinned draft initially described an earliest-to-latest default. In the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md), both pinned Besu and Nethermind builds start at head 48; Erigon and Reth start at block 1, as does the experimental Geth draft fork. An explicit head-only query succeeds on all builds. These observations establish the split, not client-team agreement on a standard.

Parity’s [original filter conversion](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L44-L68) explicitly used `Latest` for both omitted bounds; its pending fallback and address defaults are separate choices. Pinned [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/a404c4f06a67aee52cc448216b8d37a77062f106/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.JsonRpc/Modules/Trace/TraceRpcModule.cs#L278-L296) preserves that default. The live case with only `toBlock: 2` exposes the difference more clearly than an empty object: a latest implicit start at head 48 cannot reach block 2. Besu reports `-32602`, Nethermind `-32000`; the revision below fixes the code as `-32602`.

Parity could serve historical queries from an [indexed trace database](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/ethcore/trace/src/db.rs#L349-L365), whereas modern clients may replay range blocks. A [Reth operator report](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/24473) documents heavy replay load from much smaller explicit ranges. The earlier earliest-to-latest recommendation made an omitted lower bound convenient for historical search, but could turn an ordinary query into an unbounded replay. `count` limits returned records, not scan or replay work.

The historical direction is especially clear in Parity’s log filter: its [April 2016 change](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/fd2d55934b5285d213661014e064d7aa64ca497b) explicitly replaced an `earliest` default with `latest`, before the [May 2016 trace namespace introduction](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/commit/7c2adc41375d021e40c9c1e6456aeb6a8e7623a9) gave `trace_filter` latest/latest defaults from the start. Today [Ethereum.org documents](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/#eth-getlogs) `eth_getLogs` fromBlock and toBlock as latest by default, and pinned [Geth](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/572bd3696587d4f9599d577c3211c23985f7e4d1/eth/filters/api.go#L466-L482) and [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-types/src/logs_utils.rs#L156-L177) implement that choice. The current [execution-apis filter schema](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/5bcdc34a477b10af278c079525374e6a4046f291/src/schemas/filter.yaml#L13-L24) permits both fields to be omitted but does not itself declare their defaults, so the trace profile makes its choice explicit.

**Compatibility cost:** callers relying on implicit historical search in Erigon, Reth or the Geth draft fork must supply `fromBlock`. On the earlier pinned [Reth](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L352-L393), an omitted start resolved to block 0; a pruned node rejects that history and even an archive node rejects a range above its [default 100-block limit](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/4cd8f5f747ebb7fa6200bd880a2197b37cebdc1e/crates/rpc/rpc-server-types/src/constants.rs#L17-L20). Latest/latest avoids that ordinary-request failure. Explicit history must still preserve the requested start and return a pruned-history or resource-limit error if it cannot be served; it must not silently shift to the retention boundary or truncate success.

Reth main has since converged: at 861a5616 both omitted bounds default to latest ([trace.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L381-L388)), with the test `trace_filter_defaults_to_latest`. The released builds still search early history.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation required a range error for a reversed range but left its code open. Following [execution-apis #875](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/875) for eth_getLogs, the code is -32602 for reversed and beyond-head bounds alike (H06). On `h30/filter-to-2-implicit-from` Besu already returns -32602; Nethermind (-32000) and Erigon, released Reth and the Geth draft (which search early history) differ. See [filter-selection §1 and §11](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md).

items.rationale: This preserves Parity/OpenEthereum’s original trace_filter default and matches the documented eth_getLogs convention. A plain filter targets only the current head, so a small count does not leave a chain-wide range implicit or request history that may be pruned or exceed a range cap. Historical callers must name fromBlock; explicit bounds retain their meaning. On the frozen fixture, head is 48, so the omitted-bounds query matches an explicit 48-to-48 query, while toBlock 2 alone is reversed.
items.recommendation: Default omitted fromBlock and toBlock to latest, resolving both against the same canonical head at request start. An explicit toBlock older than an omitted fromBlock is a reversed range and returns -32602 (Invalid params), as does any bound that resolves beyond the current head (H06). Respect explicit endpoints, then filter and paginate the ordered range. Return 4444 when explicitly requested history is unavailable; report resource limits explicitly rather than silently narrowing the range or returning incomplete success.

background: All tested builds return NUMBER 48 for trace_callMany at explicit latest and for trace_call with omitted or explicit latest. With trace_callMany's block omitted, Besu rejects the argument count, Erigon and Nethermind return 48, and Reth returns 49. The pinned schema marks the block argument optional; see the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md).

Parity's [original `trace_callMany` implementation](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L119-L145) accepts an optional block parameter and uses the same `unwrap_or_default()` as `trace_call`; [BlockNumber's default](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/block_number.rs#L43-L47) is `Latest`. Both methods resolve a state and header for that selected block. Thus the proposed default follows the original namespace's API contract and the explicit-latest cross-client control, while Besu's argument-count failure is a request-shape incompatibility.

Pinned [Reth code](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L146-L190) deliberately defaults omitted `trace_callMany` to `BlockId::pending()` and describes sequential calls atop a pending block; its observed NUMBER 49 is consistent with a next-block environment. Choosing latest intentionally changes that established Reth default when pending differs from latest. The sequential application of calls can still work under either selector, so the issue is the omitted selector's compatibility and environment, not whether callMany is sequential.

Reth main has since converged: [d8d704cf](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/d8d704cf7d83e3b159910bd8bd0d35b41b2813cc) "fix(rpc): default trace_callMany to latest" ([#27410](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27410), 2026-09-24) uses `block_id.unwrap_or_default()` ([trace.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L157)) with the test `trace_call_many_defaults_to_latest`. The pending default described above now applies only to released builds (2.6.0 and earlier).

items.rationale: The same unsigned simulation should not silently change its block environment when batched. The frozen NUMBER constructor returns 48 at latest and 49 in Reth's pending environment, making the difference observable without mempool transactions.
items.recommendation: Make the trace_callMany block argument optional and default it to latest, matching trace_call. An explicit block selector must override that default; explicit pending is handled under H32.

background: The pinned filter schema lists earliest, finalized, safe, latest and pending, while the draft profile leaves pending-state behavior and pending localization open. In the live capture, Erigon and Nethermind resolve safe filter bounds; Besu returns -32603 and Reth -32602. Erigon development rejects pending with -32000 while its release resolves it to mined block 48. See the [live capture](../../evidence/2026-09-23/h30-code-review/README.md).

The explicit earliest-to-block-2 filter is compared with an explicit block-0-to-block-2 control. Nethermind release 2.0.0 · bec830cd returns [] for both. That is not a tag or history issue: before [Nethermind #13677](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/13677), `trace_filter` returned the records gathered so far when a block or its parent lacked state, and genesis has no parent (H06). The development build 641592d2 contains #13677 and returns the records for both. Finalized and unavailable safe/finalized were not exercised.

Parity's original pending behavior was method-specific: the [filter type](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/types/trace_filter.rs#L44-L68) warned and silently substituted `latest`; [`trace_block`](https://github.com/openethereum/parity-ethereum/blob/55c90d4016505317034e3e98f699af07f5404b63/rpc/src/v1/impls/traces.rs#L67-L78) returned `null`; simulations and replay with a pending block argument rejected it as invalid parameters. These choices predate safe/finalized selectors and did not define a shared pending state or a way to localize mined and pending trace records consistently. That history supports specifying pending per method rather than inheriting one global tag behavior.

**Recommendation risk:** explicitly rejecting pending collection requests until a contract is agreed changes Parity's historical filter fallback and `trace_block` null response. That is probably clearer to callers, but it should be recorded as a compatibility decision. The live safe-tag checks establish parsing only on available endpoints; they do not yet prove semantics for an unavailable safe/finalized head, so the recommendation's word `resolvable` matters.

### Revised recommendation (2026-09-24 source review)

The previous recommendation left pending open for every method and did not fix the selector types. The revision decides pending for historical selectors: filter bounds use the eth_getLogs `BlockNumberOrTagForRange` type, and single-block selectors reject pending as well. Current code differs widely for `trace_block("pending")`: Reth traces its locally built pending block and localizes records with that block’s hash, which is not canonical ([trace.rs](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/861a56167cd4eee8ed66e2bfb5d54a6b0620b40d/crates/rpc/rpc/src/trace.rs#L523-L560)); Besu silently uses latest; Nethermind uses its pending block; Erigon and the Geth draft return an error; Parity returned null. For filter bounds, Besu returns -32603 for safe and pending, Reth rejects earliest and safe, and Erigon’s release resolves pending to latest. `earliest` now follows the shared tag definition, which the Geth draft (mapping it to block 0 even where eth_getLogs uses the history cutoff) must change. Simulations gain block-hash selectors, which Parity, Erigon, Nethermind and Reth accept and Besu rejects. The compatibility cost against Parity’s filter fallback and `trace_block` null remains as recorded above. See [filter-selection §6 and §10](../../docs/source-review/filter-selection.md) and [simulation §5](../../docs/source-review/simulation.md).
items.next_step: Add trace_block("pending"), trace_replayBlockTransactions("pending"), block-hash simulation selectors, finalized and unavailable-finality fixtures, and a pruned filter from earliest that expects success from the retention boundary. Agree simulation pending semantics separately.
items.rationale: A caller must be able to tell whether a tag was rejected, resolved to a mined block, or evaluated in a pending environment. In the frozen fixture, safe resolves to head 48, while Reth's pending call environment exposes NUMBER 49. These observations do not establish mempool transaction inclusion.
items.recommendation: trace_filter bounds use BlockNumberOrTagForRange: earliest, latest, safe and finalized are accepted, pending returns -32602, and earliest means the lowest block the client has available. trace_block and trace_replayBlockTransactions also reject pending with -32602 until a pending contract exists; localized records never carry a block hash that is not canonical. trace_call and trace_callMany accept a block number, tag or block hash (BlockNumberOrTagOrHash). Pending for simulations remains unspecified: a client that does not implement it must reject it explicitly, and a valid tag must not produce an internal error. Resolve selectors against one consistent chain view for the request.
